packet.title: Self-trial hardening: evidence identity, reason codes, path rebinding, runtime_ref, derived amendment
packet.objective: Close the mechanical findings of the first self-hosting trial: every denial carries a stable policy code; platform-absolute paths rebind to workspace-relative form before policy runs; guard, obligation, and gate events bind the admitted packet identity, a unique attempt id, and a logical action id; the generated hooks derive a per-session run identity and the commit gate fails closed on the unbound fallback; whether a packet amends enforcement is derived from its write scope against the protected set, which the spec extends with the workspace TCB; every event carries runtime_ref binding playbook, kernel, and envelope ABI into one constitutional identity, reported as segments by ledger verify.
constraints: No weakening of any existing guarantee: the full workspace test suite must remain green
Chained ledger history stays frozen — new fields default to explicit legacy emptiness, no rewrite of transition strings
Generated artifacts change only via the spec and harnessc build, never by hand
acceptance_criteria: Every denial event in a fresh ledger carries a policy:<code> evidence ref
An absolute path inside the workspace is allowed when its relative form is in scope, and the event records both spellings
A packet writing crates/kernel/ with amends_enforcement=false is refused admission with enforcement.amendment_undeclared
kernel ledger verify prints runtime segments and events carry runtime_ref
A git commit under run id 'unknown' is denied with policy:identity.run_unbound

packet.title: Constitutional succession: govern the replacement of the governor
packet.objective: Implement the succession protocol designed in docs/SUCCESSION.md: kernel succession disarm/activate subcommands writing gate-bound transition events; a succession manifest binding old_runtime_ref, old_ledger_head, maintenance task, patch and conformance digests, new_kernel_ref, and approver identity; ledger verify flagging runtime-segment boundaries that lack an attesting succession.activate record; and a versioned conformance fixture matrix a candidate kernel must pass before activation.
constraints: Every activation requires a signature-authenticated human approval — the running kernel never approves its own successor
History predating the protocol stays legible: unattested legacy boundaries warn, they do not fail
Compose the existing gate, signature, and anchoring primitives; introduce no new trust machinery
acceptance_criteria: A full disarm→repair→conformance→approve→activate cycle on a fixture workspace leaves a ledger whose runtime boundary carries an attesting succession.activate event linking the old chain head
gate verify refuses activation when the manifest's action hash no longer matches the manifest bytes
ledger verify warns on a runtime-segment boundary with no succession attestation

packet.title: Perform the first attested succession (runtime 02a6c163 -> c70149d8)
packet.objective: Attest the seating of the succession-protocol kernel (merged PR #24, maintenance packet a6b89a7737f0) as a governed constitutional transition: author the succession manifest from recorded ledger fact, bind it through the gate, approve it with an Ed25519 signature registered to the repository owner, run the conformance matrix as a precondition, and activate so the runtime boundary at record 69 carries an approved attestation.
constraints: The record-17 boundary is history and stays unattested — the protocol never manufactures governance retroactively
The approver private seed never enters the repository; only the public registry is committed
acceptance_criteria: kernel ledger verify no longer warns on the record-69 boundary and still warns on record 17
The succession manifest and approver registry are committed
